decision: The predeclared short-horizon gate passes on both valid 50/50 expert/replay seeds. Under deployment-feasible current-buffer GAR, seed 0 and seed 1 respectively achieve positive four-step normalized edit-distance improvement (0.0630 and 0.0633), positive mean selected true advantage (0.195 and 0.188), and beat the matched target-free random control (-0.364 on both); all expected artifacts are present, there are no NaNs or invalid actions, and neither trajectory loops. Full-horizon diagnostics independently show a reproducible boundary: decisions 1-2 are positive, decisions 3-4 are near neutral, and decision 5 is negative on both seeds (-0.313 and -0.281). Evaluate the two fixed checkpoints at horizons 2 and 5 to determine whether four decisions are a stable useful operating point or a cutoff-sensitive result. Treat the boundary as established only if both seeds improve over their matched random controls at both horizons, horizon 2 is positive, and horizon 5 is worse than horizon 4; otherwise inspect episode-level paired failure strata before changing training. No checkpoint is trained or selected in this round. Proposal generation and GAR selection remain target-free; terminal targets are used only for separately labelled test metrics, and oracle-injected conditions remain candidate-privileged diagnostics.
